温かく glossed 'warm, lukewarm': 'lukewarm' corresponds to ぬるい and is nearly the opposite of what is requested here (making the coffee properly warm/hot).

Locale-parity gap in the applied fix. The op removed 'lukewarm' from the en gloss because it is 'nearly the opposite of what is requested here (making the coffee properly warm/hot)', giving 'warm (pleasantly hot)'. The pt gloss was left as 'quente (agradável), ameno', and 'ameno' carries exactly the mild/tepid nuance that was just rejected in English — it also fights the record's own lit_pt 'torna

The repair replaced 'quente (agradável), ameno' with 'quente (agradavelmente quente)', which is circular: the parenthetical that is supposed to disambiguate just repeats the head word ('quente ... quente'). It teaches nothing and, unlike the en counterpart 'warm (pleasantly hot)', fails to separate 温かい from 熱い. A gloss that defines a word with itself should not ship.
